pick.name: Playwright CLI + skills (Microsoft)
pick.what: Browser automation CLI with skills for coding agents
pick.why: Microsoft's own README says CLI+skills is more token-efficient than MCP for coding agents; headless works without GPU

alts.name: Playwright MCP
alts.why: Use for exploratory/self-healing loops that need persistent state

alts.name: Chrome DevTools MCP (Google)
alts.what: Perf traces, network, console with source maps; CLI + 7 skills

candidates.name: agent-browser (Vercel)
candidates.verdict: Rust CLI, 44.7k stars, strong but less mature test ecosystem

candidates.name: browser-use
candidates.verdict: Python agent framework, not a test tool

decision: Your E2E tests should be Playwright anyway, so the same tool verifying Claude's UI work is the lowest-friction choice; CLI mode keeps context small. Add Chrome DevTools MCP when chasing performance.

verify.note: README does say 'CLI invocations are more token-efficient: they avoid loading large tool schemas' (claim holds, it is Microsoft's own claim, not a benchmark). npm @playwright/cli is still 0.x: 0.1.22 published 2026-09-28. source_url points at playwright-mcp; use the CLI repo.
